newsitems.title: Update 2 is LIVE! See the full patch notes / changelist here.
newsitems.author: GSG Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/8803f0aea75d16660ea3447bc6077dee7f53f684.png[/img]

[h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1]

Welcome to Update 2 of Rogue Core early access! We’ve implemented some core (ha) difficulty changes in this one along with a bunch of tweaks and fixes and of course some new content. Much to get through, so we plopped it all in a big list down below.

As always, we look forward to hearing your feedback. <3 [b]Rock and Stone![/b]

[i]With love,
- The Ghost Ship crew[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h2][b]--- PATCH NOTES ---[/b][/h2]

[h3][b]THREAT LEVELS[/b][/h3]
You can now tailor the base difficulty of the game to your liking using the new ‘Threat Level’ difficulty scale. There are five Threat Levels, and they affect the number of enemies, the frequency of swarms, enemy health and movement, enemy aggression (attack frequency and projectile speed) and overall damage.
This should give you more control over your gameplay experience, letting you play most of the game’s content at a difficulty of your preference. It also means that Depth is now purely geared as a content progression tree, rather than affecting difficulty.

[h3][b]UNGATED SERVERLIST[/b][/h3]
Most of the restrictions from the Server Browser have been removed to make it easier to find a lobby. You can now join missions that may be at Depths or in biomes that you haven’t yet unlocked. You still need to unlock a Depth to be able to host missions there, however.

[h3][b]WAVE STACKING[/b][/h3]
We have also officially added the possibility for the stage’s waves to stack on Threat Levels 4 and 5. This is something that was happening unintentionally for quite a long time due to a bug, but it is now implemented as a feature for higher difficulties.

[h3][b]NO BOSS INVULNERABILITY[/b][/h3]
We're getting rid of the bosses’ invulnerability phases triggered by taking loads of damage in a short time. Instead, bosses will either do a very short block, or attempt to block in a way that can still be managed via careful aim, AoE damage or repositioning. Hopefully this makes it feel like more of a fair fight.

[h3][b]NEW UPGRADES[/b][/h3]
The pool of Expenite Upgrades has been further expanded with a focus on elemental damage types. Seven new Expenite Upgrades and one new Artifact are coming in Update 2:
[olist]
[*] [b]Spark-Booster:[/b] When enemies in medium range are electrocuted, you get 45% movement speed for +3 seconds.
[*] [b]Grid-Shock:[/b] Damaging electrified targets spreads +50% as electric damage to other enemies connected via electrical arcs.
[*] [b]Weathering Blast:[/b] When active Stone Skin expires, deal 50 Ice damage in short range. +25 additional damage per 5 Stone Skin lost.
[*] [b]Icy Shrapnel:[/b] Hitting frozen targets launches ice fractures in the opposite direction, dealing +25% Ice damage in a Short Range cone.
[*] [b]Icicle Strike:[/b] Power Attacks spawn icicles lasting for +5s.
[*] [b]Concussive Shot:[/b] Weakpoint hits have 25% chance to stun targets for +2 seconds. Stun is guaranteed when destroying breakable weakpoints and doubles duration.
[*] [b]Frostbane:[/b] For every active Stone Skin you get +5% Ice bonus on all melee damage.
[*] [b][ARTIFACT] Nuclear Optics:[/b] Enemies in your flashlight beam take 30 Radiation damage per second. 
[/olist]
[h3][b]NEW ARTIFACT EVENT[/b][/h3]
A new event has been added to the pool of possible stage spawns, but this one gets you an Artifact instead of Expenite. You’ll need to reactivate a classified experiment and see if you can’t finish what R&D started before they were forced to abandon the project. Hope you brought your thinking caps.

[h3][b]NEW ALTERATIONS[/b][/h3]
We’re adding four new Alterations to give more gameplay variety to your missions.
[olist]
[*] [b]High Stakes:[/b] Increased Luck in equipment & upgrade RNG, but reduced Expenite gains from all sources.
[*] [b]Siege Engines:[/b] All enemies (except bosses) move at half speed and have twice as much health.
[*] [b]Headhunter:[/b] Expenite does not spawn in the caves, but all enemies drop Expenite on death.
[*] [b]Death Mitosis:[/b] All Core Spawn split into two smaller ‘baby zombies’ when killed. All enemies (except bosses) have less health.
[/olist]
[h3][b]NEW OLD WEAPON: LOK-1 SMART RIFLE[/b][/h3]
The Engineer’s Smart Rifle from DRG is now part of the standard weapon pool. It’s taken some work to get this weapon’s unique auto-lock firing mechanism to work with Rogue Core’s upgrades and damage systems, but now it’s tested and combat-ready.

[h3][b]NEW ENEMY: VOIDKIN DOMINATOR[/b][/h3]
A long-range threat is coming to the mines: the Voidkin Dominator. It’s a tankier, harder-hitting version of its smaller cousin, the Drifter. The Dominator targets foes with hard-hitting projectiles that leave volatile Rift energy lingering in the area of impact. On death, the Dominator releases its internal energy reserves, resulting in an intense explosion.

[h3][b]NEW ENTRANCE FACILITIES + CAVE GENERATION[/b][/h3]
Rogue Core's cave generation system has been expanded with 4 new facility entrance rooms and 15 new cavern formations. We’ve also reworked the cave generator’s process for connecting individual caverns.

[h3][b]NEW MOLAKTULA BIOME[/b][/h3]
The Molaktula Gatekeeper boss now has a new home with some explosive gravity defying elements. Now each of the 3 Gatekeepers have their own corresponding biome on their respective depth. As we add more Gatekeepers in the future, they too will get a biome to call their own. 

[h3][b]ALPHA CLEARANCE GRANTED[/b][/h3]
All Reclaimers have been automatically granted Security Clearance Level Alpha within the Intel system. This means that brand new players will no longer be locked out of starting Expenite Events or opening the Grenade Locker during their first missions.

[h3][b]COMBAT AND BALANCE[/b][/h3]
- Fusion Rod now works with ammo pool upgrades and clip size upgrades 
- Removed the ‘double mag’ attribute from the Devastator
- Increase Heavy Landing minimum radius from 1m to 2m
- Impact Axes are back in the Grenade Locker
- Removed the Burst Fire upgrade from the Hammercaster
- Temporarily removed the ‘Return to Sender’ upgrade from the Breach Cutter until it is fixed

- Killing blows with the pickaxe no longer slow the player down
- Sped up the spawning of enemies in waves when enemies are cleared fast, allowing the whole wave to be completed faster
- Rifts now spawn and follow the player for each wave, so enemies try to spawn close to the player. NowhereToRun.mp3
- Slightly extended minimum time between waves
- Shotguns no longer trigger Lucky Shot multiple times
- Change ‘Duck and Weave’ to provide its block chance when jumping or sprinting
- Added more Red Sugar to the Gatekeeper’s cave
- Added 1 second more grace time for players to revive before the run fails

[h3][b]VOICELINES / LASER POINTER[/b][/h3]
We did a big pass of writing and recording hundreds of more voicelines, with the main goal of making the laser pointer much more useful in directing teammates’ attention toward relevant objectives.

- Added laser pointer voicelines for pinging basically all mission/gameplay-relevant objects

[h3][b]MISCELLANEOUS[/b][/h3]

newsitems.title: UPDATE 2 PREVIEW
newsitems.author: GSG Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/98c61814c8642e9c133a6c9fc6b5c123c6b4ae14.jpg"][/img]
[/p][h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1][p]
Update 2 is just around the corner — it’ll go live in Rogue Core on [b]Wednesday, September 2nd[/b] at [b]13:00 CEST[/b]. Here’s your first look at what’s coming.

We’ll post the full patch notes when the update goes live next week. This preview will focus more closely at the biggest changes and additions, and our thoughts behind them. Bug fixes, balance tweaks, QoL improvements and smaller stuff like that will go in those patch notes.

If you’d like to get your hands on all of this before next week’s release, it's now live in the Experimental Branch! Instructions on how to activate that are at the bottom of this post.

[/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h2][b]NEW DIFFICULTY SYSTEM: THREAT LEVELS[/b][/h2][p]As part of making it easier to tailor the Rogue Core experience to your own tastes, we’re implementing a new difficulty system.

With Update 1, we introduced the ‘Assault Pace’ setting to allow more options for adjusting the mission timer. Now, we’re introducing the ‘Threat Level’ difficulty scale. This will uncouple the game difficulty from the chosen Depth. It also means game difficulty is now totally independent from the mission timer, giving you more fine-tuned control over your own game experience.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/be9f2e6a624f8f4f06061b840e6572a284427bdf.png"][/img][/p][p]In Update 2, you’ll see the screen above upon selecting a mission. This big screen will just show up once, and after that the Threat Level will join the Assault Pace toggle over on the right side of the screen.  [/p][p]Here’s how the new setup works:[/p][list][*][p][b][u]Threat Level:[/u][/b] The five Threat Levels affect the number of enemies, the frequency of swarms, enemy health and movement, enemy aggression (attack frequency and projectile speed) and overall damage.[/p][/*][*][p][b][u]Assault Pace:[/u][/b] This adjusts the pacing of your run, by adding more or less time to the mission timer. Tone it down if you like taking your time, ramp it up if you work best on a deadline.[/p][/*][*][p][b][u]Depth:[/u][/b] With these changes, Depth now only determines access to certain bosses (and the associated boss biome). We’re making it more of a progression system for game content, rather than necessarily being tied to the mission timer and difficulty level. For this reason we have temporarily locked Depth 4 until the fourth boss is ready. Stay tuned![/p][/*][/list][p]This system will be available from the start of the game. So if you’re someone who finds Rogue Core too difficult, you’ll be able to play through all the game’s content at a gentler difficulty. And if you think Rogue Core is too easy, you can start right at a high difficulty without having to grind to unlock later Depths. Mostly. To join or host a mission on the maximum “Hellish” Threat Level 5 you’ll need to beat a run on Threat Level 4 first, just to prove you can hang with the big dogs.

We hope this addition gives everyone more options to play Rogue Core how they want. We’ve gotten good feedback on this from the Experimental testers so far, and we’ll be watching and listening to take in your thoughts.

[/p][h2][b]UNGATED SERVERLIST (MORE MATCHMAKING)[/b][/h2][p]Uncoupling Depth Level from overall difficulty also opens up for expanded matchmaking options, meaning more options for you to join a lobby or a game in progress. 

With an ungated serverlist, you can now join missions that may be at Depths that you haven’t yet unlocked. Previously these would have been off-limits, shrinking your pool of joinable options. In otherwords, more matchmaking for everybody. If you’d like to [i]host[/i] missions in certain biomes or Depths, you’ll still need to unlock them yourself.

[/p][h2][b]BOSS INVULNERABILITY PHASES REMOVED[/b][/h2][p]In response to player feedback, we're getting rid of the bosses’ long invulnerability phases in response to taking loads of damage in a short time. Instead, bosses will either do a very short block, or attempt to block in a way that can still be managed via careful aim, AoE damage or repositioning. Hopefully this makes it feel like more of a fair fight.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/780b746e1d7916579391800284f81c053c12e79a.gif"][/img][/p][h2][b]NEW UPGRADES + ARTIFACT[/b][/h2][p]We’re expanding the pool of Expenite Upgrades yet again, this time with a focus on elemental damage types. Seven new Expenite Upgrades and one new Artifact are coming in Update 2:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Spark-Booster:[/b] When enemies in medium range are electrocuted, you get 45% movement speed for +3 seconds.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Grid-Shock:[/b] Damaging electrified targets spreads +50% as electric damage to other enemies connected via electrical arcs.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Weathering Blast:[/b] When active Stone Skin expires, deal 50 Ice damage in short range. +25 additional damage per 5 Stone Skin lost.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Icy Shrapnel:[/b] Hitting frozen targets launches ice fractures in the opposite direction, dealing +25% Ice damage in a Short Range cone. [/p][/*][*][p][b]Icicle Strike:[/b] Power Attacks spawn icicles lasting for +5s.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Concussive Shot:[/b] Weakpoint hits have 25% chance to stun targets for +2 seconds. Stun is guaranteed when destroying breakable weakpoints and doubles duration.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Frostbane:[/b] For every active Stone Skin you get +5% Ice bonus on all melee damage.[/p][/*][*][p][b]\[ARTIFACT] Nuclear Optics:[/b] Enemies in your flashlight beam take 30 Radiation damage per second.
[/p][/*][/olist][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/6277eb1115248dc73631fbe6eaaa8c01e0d5c303.png"][/img][/p][h2][b]NEW ARTIFACT EVENT[/b][/h2][p]We’ve got a new encounter down in the caves: an unfinished, highly-classified research site left behind by R&D. This is a new event which can grant you an Artifact, which has a random chance to spawn instead of an Expenite Event. You don’t have to select the ‘Artifact’ Mission Alteration in order to encounter it.

You’ll need to reactivate the experiment and see if you can’t finish what R&D started, before they were forced to abandon the project. OMEGA will guide you along the way.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/51962573017bbf96a3775222a9b283a26f570b8d.gif"][/img][/p][h2][b]NEW ALTERATIONS[/b][/h2][p]Based on player enthusiasm about the ‘Jumble’ Alteration, we’re adding four new Alterations to give more gameplay variety to your missions:[/p][olist][*][p][b]High Stakes:[/b] Increased Luck in upgrade RNG, but reduced Expenite gains from all sources.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Siege Engines:[/b] All enemies (except bosses) move at half speed and have twice as much health.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Headhunter:[/b] Expenite does not spawn in the caves, but all enemies drop Expenite on death.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Death Mitosis:[/b] All Core Spawn split into two smaller ‘baby zombies’ when killed. All enemies (except bosses) have less health.
[/p][/*][/olist][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/c64899f39363401c40ed6ef9e18f38409ae88666.png"][/img][/p][h2][b]NEW OLD WEAPON: LOK-1 SMART RIFLE[/b][/h2][p]The Engineer’s Smart Rifle from DRG is now part of the standard weapon pool. It’s taken some work to get this weapon’s unique auto-lock firing mechanism to work with Rogue Core’s player upgrades and damage systems, but now it’s tested and combat-ready. It’ll probably be really good at taking out those pesky Boomticks. Let us know what you think.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/5a02ac77314f6601b002f2c5c84edee7de2d8569.gif"][/img][/p][h2][b]NEW ENEMY: VOIDKIN DOMINATOR[/b][/h2][p]A long-range threat is coming to the mines. Meet the Voidkin Dominator, a tankier, harder-hitting version of its smaller cousin, the Drifter. Consider this a high-priority target.

The Reclaimer’s Handbook reads:
[/p][code]"The Dominator exists as a living siphon of Rift energy, corrupting its body in the process. Little is known about this creature in an adolescent state, before exposure to extreme Rift radiation. It is able to target foes with hard-hitting projectiles that leave volatile Rift energy lingering in the area of impact. 

On death, the Dominator releases its internal energy reserves, resulting in an intense explosion. Keep your distance."[/code][p]
[/p][carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/5a013e10f62a7b7edb95c34fe0ecb3e5172774d4.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/52f134a5872bff468fee09d2deb15df4c63ba324.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/e126c8de145968cd998d50d057bf732940125e1b.png"][/img][/carousel][h2][b]NEW ENTRANCE FACILITIES + CAVE GENERATION[/b][/h2][p]We’ve added 3 new facility entrance rooms (the place where you select your first weapon) and 15 new cavern formations to the cave generation system. We’ve also reworked the cave generator’s process for connecting individual caverns, so this will hopefully result in more variety in the physical layout of each level.  [/p][p][/p][h2][b]NEW MOLAKTULA BIOME[/b][/h2][p]We’re putting together a new home for the Molaktula Gatekeeper boss, so now each of the Gatekeepers bosses have their own corresponding biome. Like the others, this biome should ‘bleed’ into the original mission biome more and more as you venture further down. Our intent here is to give each boss and Depth a more distinct identity, and more visual variety between missions. [/p][p][/p][h2][b]ALPHA CLEARANCE AUTO-GRANTED[/b][/h2][p]All Reclaimers have been automatically granted Security Clearance Level Alpha within the Intel system. This means that brand new players will no longer be locked out of starting Expenite Events or opening the Grenade Locker during their first missions. [/p][p]Maybe this is a smaller thing but hey it’s in the post now.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][h1][b]How to access the Experimental Branch[/b][/h1][p]
Like we said up top, all of this is currently live over in Experimental. We’ve started running Experimental Branch for longer periods of time, with the aim of collecting feedback on gameplay systems with enough time to make tweaks and rebalances. Much of Update 2 has already been shaped and sharpened by the feedback of our brave Experimental testers. If you’ve got the time and interest, you’re very welcome to hop in and give it a go.

Anybody can access the Experimental Branch if they own Rogue Core on Steam. 
Here’s how to set it live:
[/p][olist][*][p] Right click Rogue Core in your Steam library and select ‘Properties’
[/p][/*][*][p] Under ‘Properties,’ click the ‘Game Versions & Betas’ tab
[/p][/*][*][p] Select ‘experimental’ within that tab
[/p][/*][/olist][p]Then the game will update and will boot into the Experimental branch next time you launch it. You can switch back any time through the same menu. Keep in mind that your [b]save files from the Experimental branch don’t carry over[/b], because we have cheats enabled there.

[/p][hr][/hr][p]Looking forward to hearing your thoughts! Again, the full run-down of everything new (even the little stuff, of which there is plenty) is coming in the patch notes when Update 2 goes live. Which is next week on Wednesday September 2nd. At 13:00 CEST right after we eat our lunch.

[b]Rock and Stone, Reclaimers![/b]

[i]With love,
-The Ghost Ship Crew[/i]

newsitems.author: Julie - GSG
newsitems.contents:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/7eba779cfa134d329a48e3768e0f3c4dc9d9a698.jpg"][/img][b]PATCH NOTES: \[ RC: EA: 01.03 - 148107][/b]  [/p][h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1][p]

newsitems.title: Beefy bosses and disconnect insurance: Update 1.2 explained
newsitems.author: GSG Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/f89f9f0d1cc24bd927a5c329f7a2cf341be69790.jpg[/img][h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1]

Lead Game Designer Mike here. With this week's Update 1.2 turning out quite large, we thought a more feature-focused version of the patch notes would help shine some light on the 'what' and 'why' of this update. Some of the changes have some more significant effects on the gameplay experience, so I think that’s worth looking at in detail.

You can find the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2605790/view/699891276559941795?l=english]full 1.2 patch notes linked right here[/url], and our explanations right down below.

Let’s get to it.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Balancing player power and game difficulty[/h2]

With Update 1 players can more consistently reach higher power levels, which is good. It has become easier to trigger synergies and deal big damage. Currently certain systems (like crit damage and fire) are overrepresented in the upgrade pool, but this will even out as we add more upgrades and artifacts that work with the other elements of the damage system. However, the game needs to respond accordingly and many of the changes in Patch 1.2 focus on how the game can better test this power. 

[h2]Difficulty and Risk Vectors[/h2]

We really like the Risk Vector system as it gives a bit of agency in how the game's difficulty increases. Some allow you to increase the spice, others give you some benefits that make it a bit easier. This was not always the case however, as some Risk Vectors had almost no impact on the run. We have fixed and tweaked all the Risk Vectors that bring enemies into the run (like Edgestalker Patrol and Scorcher Horde) to make sure their impact is felt. Selecting these Risk Vectors and especially stacking them now has very real consequences, which is how we want it.

[h2]Beefier bosses[/h2]

With Patch 1.2 we focused on making sure the Gatekeepers (AKA the bosses) can better withstand high-powered players. It’s fun to wreck a boss, but it’s even more fun if the boss tries to fight back in the process and can still pose a threat. Each Gatekeeper type now has counterattacks that they can perform to reduce pressure (on themselves) and temporarily block some or all of the player’s attacks while still applying pressure back on the Reclaimers. We also tweaked Gatekeeper health scaling to keep pace with the players’ power growth on 5- and 6-stage missions. And in relation to the previously mentioned Risk Vectors, they now also have an impact on the boss fight by adding their spawns to the pool of enemies that assist the Gatekeepers.

[h2]More Reaperworm pressure[/h2]

Staying around when the threat level becomes critical is not something Reclaimers should take lightly. To more strongly encourage teams to get on the elevator, we now spawn more additional Reaperworms over time, starting roughly 30 seconds after the first worms appear. The exact rate depends on the number of players. (This change was missing from the original patch notes.)

[h2]Safeguarding from disconnects[/h2]

In the event that a mission abruptly ends (whether due to a crash, a disconnect or getting rudely kicked from the team) you will now be awarded the XP rewards and bonuses you have earned up to that point, making sure that your time was not completely wasted.

[hr][/hr]
That’s the main stuff! Again, the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2605790/view/699891276559941795?l=english]full patch notes are right here[/url] if you want to give them a look. But these are the key changes that we felt deserved a bit more explanation.

The next two weeks we'll be closed for the summer holidays. When we're back we'll continue working on Update 2, which we expect to have out in August. Hope everybody's having a nice summer. Rock and Stone!

[i]With love,
-The Ghost Ship Crew[/i]

newsitems.title: Update 01 is live! See the full patch notes here.
newsitems.author: GSG Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[previewyoutube="0Y-8LzUlWOM;full"][/previewyoutube][h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1][p]
We're excited to launch the first major Update for Rogue Core! After much consideration, we have decided to call this first update 'Update 01'. 

It's been a busy couple weeks leading up to this. We've been doing a lot of experimenting, tweaking and adjusting, including some big revamps to core game mechanics. We also squeezed in some new content for good measure. There's a lot in here. Mark made (and narrated) a trailer to explain everything, which you can watch via the embedded link above. Otherwise, you'll find the full list of changes and additions down below.

As always, your feedback is integral to our development process, so remember to [url="https://discord.com/invite/drg"]join our Discord[/url] or hop on the [url="https://www.reddit.com/r/RogueCore/"]Rogue Core subreddit[/url] and let us know what you think.

Welcome to Update 01! Let's get right into it.

[/p][hr][/hr][h1][b]--- GAMEPLAY UPDATES ---[/b][/h1][p]
[/p][h2]Improved mission timer[/h2][p]
We've updated the mission timer's UI to better communicate what's happening during a run.
[/p][list][*][p] Improved timer feedback and readability[/p][/*][*][p] The last segment of the timer is now visually distinct to communicate urgency[/p][/*][*][p] Optional numerical countdown showing exactly when Reaperworms will appear
[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/9bfcced185df0777df846506138fb8c40a97bc31.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Assault Pace selection[/h2][p]
To accommodate different player preferences for mission pacing, you can now select your preferred [b]Assault Pace[/b] directly from the Mission Map. Adjusting the Assault Pace affects the time you have to complete each level and the mission XP rewards. Base reward values have been adjusted to accommodate these changes. We have also added new Tasks in the OpsCom terminal for each Pace.

You can choose from three Assault Pace options:
[/p][olist][*][p][b]Cautious[/b] – Lower time pressure[/p][/*][*][p][b]Standard[/b] – Current experience[/p][/*][*][p][b]Reckless[/b] – Higher time pressure
[/p][/*][/olist][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/ce40e3575d98e68c5cf78d138a618a6b78a37513.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]R.E.P.D. upgrade process improvements[/h2][p]
Initiating upgrades at the R.E.P.D. has been streamlined, so you no longer need to group up to start the process. This change applies to upgrades from Expenite as well as Spectre Cores. 

Here's how it works now:
[/p][olist][*][p] When an upgrade becomes available, a button will appear on the R.E.P.D.[/p][/*][*][p] Any Reclaimer can press it to initiate the upgrade process.[/p][/*][*][p] An upgrade link will be established with all Reclaimers on the team, regardless of their location.
[/p][/*][/olist][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/00fc16bcbad688c9c6916c1430259023a4289c5c.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]Upgrade negotiations rework[/h2][p]
We've made several improvements to the shared upgrade negotiation process, to make things more fun and give everyone more choices. We've been having a lot of fun with these changes ourselves, and we're keen to hear what you think.

Here are the key changes to upgrade negotiations:
[/p][list][*][p] When a player selects an upgrade, it is replaced with a new option. This ensures everyone gets the same number of choices.[/p][/*][*][p] The "Skip for Health" option has been removed. (Don't worry, we've made balances to account for this. More on that later.)[/p][/*][*][p] Health upgrades now appear alongside all other upgrades.[/p][/*][*][p] All upgrades within a draft now share the same rarity. Either you all luck out together, or you all pick between common upgrades.
[/p][/*][/list][p]We have also tweaked many of the existing upgrades, changing some of them extensively and removing others to make every choice feel exciting and worthwhile. This will be an ongoing process, so consider this just a first iteration.

[/p][hr][/hr][h1][b]--- NEW CONTENT ---[/b][/h1][p]
[/p][h2]New weapons[/h2][list][*][p][b]Trident \[Energy shotgun][/b]: A new weapon from the makers of the DRAK 25, the Trident offers two firing modes: Standard fire is a semi-automatic blast in a triangle shot pattern. Holding down the trigger will charge up a massive barrage for dealing with groups of targets, or inflicting devastating single-target damage.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Corrosive Sludge Pump \[Heavy weapon][/b]: Looks like goop is back on the menu. Offering a mix of crowd control and continuous DoT, the Sludge Pump is a versatile weapon that also excels at melting enemy armor. The weapon can be charged to lob a large projectile saturating an area in corrosive sludge.
[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/6295b3742dcc1c3aea8df536e23ece8cfa0f158a.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]New Expenite Upgrades[/h2][p]
Besides tweaking existing upgrades, we have also introduced 14 new ones to add more variety and spice to your builds. We are far from finished here, so you can expect ongoing balance tweaks as well as new additions to the upgrade pool in later updates.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/07241fc3c22fb1b0c5808e2271a983ef2c55a302.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]New airborne enemy[/h2][p]
You'll now have to contend with the [b]Voidkin Drifter,[/b] a brand-new flying threat to expand the combat variety. Highly mobile and hard to hit, the Drifter will only stop to charge up its ranged attack. While the Void Bolts it launches may be relatively slow, they pack a heavy punch. So watch out and don’t let yourself get surrounded.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/f7102c2b9e1a780d99d044da2a3d3a1216f12845.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]New Risk Vectors[/h2][p]
We have added 3 new Risk Vectors to the pool of possible choices, with one being negative and and the other two positive.
[/p][olist][*][p] Drifter Surge \[Negative]: Brings in additional groups of the new Voidkin during your run.[/p][/*][*][p] Bio-Booster \[Positive]: Adds a second Bio-Booster to the level.[/p][/*][*][p] Workbench \[Positive]: Adds a second Workbench to the level.
[/p][/*][/olist][h2]New Core Biome[/h2][p]
Our goal is to introduce a unique Core biome for each end boss.

With Update 01, we're adding a new Core biome for the Ramok boss, to give that fight experience a more distinct atmosphere and identity. For now, our friend the Molaktula will also use this biome until its own unique environment arrives in a future update.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/a80458ad4faecfa79a3d7db9e2aa121160ae089c.jpg"][/img][/p][h2]New mining constructions[/h2][p]
We've implemented 13 new mining constructions to the cave generation system, which ought to bring greater variety to facility exploration.

[/p][h2]New OpsCom Deployments and Tasks[/h2][p]
We have added 2 new Deployments to the OpsCom terminal. For both, you can progress in these challenges even without achieving total mission success.
[/p][list][*][p][b]Eliminate Corespawn:[/b] Tracked as a team, not individual kills.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Clear Facility Levels:[/b] Sometimes just making it one level deeper is a hard-fought win.
[/p][/*][/list][p]We have also added 3 new Tasks, one for each Assault Pace.

[/p][hr][/hr][h1][b]--- WEAPON BALANCE ---[/b][/h1][p]
We're making a broad pass on weapon balance and weapon selection pools, with the aim of making a more consistent difficulty floor across the game. Changes are as follows:
[/p][list][*][p] All starting weapons are now common, but come with 2 attributes.[/p][/*][*][p] Workbenches now have a chance for offering higher rarity weapons and traversal tools.[/p][/*][*][p] Heavy Weapon Crates now have a wider rarity range.[/p][/*][*][p] Additionally, several harder-to-master weapons (like the Shock Striker and Devastator) have been removed from the starting weapon pool on Depth 1, allowing new players to ease into the experience more naturally. They can still be found in the Workbench, and are still part of the starting pool on all other Depths.
[/p][/*][/list][p]A few individual weapons are getting balance tweaks as well. Tthis will be an ongoing process and feedback is always appreciated:
[/p][list][*][p] Reduced base spread of the Boomstick[/p][/*][*][p] Slightly reduced base damage of the Boomstick, [i]but[/i] increased the number of pellets in a shell. This increases the overall damage done by one shot.[/p][/*][*][p] Slightly reduced the max recoil of the Decker SMG[/p][/*][*][p] Slightly increased base damage on the M1000[/p][/*][*][p] Increased the focus speed and added a damage bonus to focus shots on the M1000[/p][/*][*][p] Significantly increased the explosion damage of the PGL and reduced max ammo slightly to compensate[/p][/*][*][p] Set Warthog to be full-auto by default[/p][/*][*][p] Increased base damage on the Warthog slightly
[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h1][b]--- BUG FIXES AND OPTIMIZATION ---[/b][/h1][p]
We've been doing a lot of tinkering to support general performance optimisation, both on the Ramrod and during missions. This includes a lot of specific optimisation for the myriad of particle systems, as these can get pretty hefty.
 
We also squashed a lot of bugs, including but not limited to:

newsitems.title: Experimental Live - Update 1 coming June 17
newsitems.author: GSG Lars
newsitems.contents:
[h1][b]EXPERIMENTAL LIVE[/b][/h1][p][b]
Update 1 Release:[/b] June 17[/p][p]
Hi Reclaimers,[/p][p]The wait is over! We're finally ready to open up the EXPERIMENTAL BRANCH for Rogue Core. If you're interested in getting an early look at what's coming in UPDATE 1, now is your chance to jump in and help us test what's ahead!  

[b]HOW TO ACCESS THE EXPERIMENTAL BRANCH[/b][/p][olist][*][p]Right-click on Rogue Core in your Steam Library >[/p][/*][*][p]Click “Properties..” >[/p][/*][*][p]Select “Betas” >[/p][/*][*][p]Click the drop-down menu under "Beta Participation" >[/p][/*][*][p]Select “experimental - WIP build - enter at own risk![/p][/*][*][p]Then wait for the game to update (Restart Steam and/or Verify Game Files to be 100% sure). Welcome to EXPERIMENTAL![/p][/*][/olist][p][b]
WHAT TO EXPECT FROM EXPERIMENTAL?[/b][/p][p]The Experimental Branch contains work-in-progress content for UPDATE 1. Things are still under active development, so expect bugs, crashes, balance issues, and unfinished features. Please keep that in mind while testing and sharing feedback.  
 [/p][p][b]WHY DO WE HAVE AN EXPERIMENTAL BRANCH?[/b][/p][p]The Experimental Branch lets us test new content at a much larger scale and gives us the opportunity to balance, tweak, and fix issues before they make it into the live game.[/p][p]You can participate in discussions, share feedback, and report bugs in the [url="https://discord.com/channels/257785731072786435/1514553034410299472"]Experimental Branch channel[/url] on our [url="https://discord.com/channels/257785731072786435/1514553034410299472"]Discord server[/url].[/p][p][/p][p]All feedback is welcome and helps make Rogue Core better. Thank you for being part of the process! [/p][p][i]Please note that any progress on the Experimental Branch is not carrying over into your live savegame![/i][/p][p][i]Please note that we had to last-minute-pull the new biome for the Ramok and The Molaktula from the Experimental Build due to shenanigans with it. We will add it as soon as it is ready![/i]
[/p][hr][/hr][p]
Here is an overview of what you can experience on the Experimental Branch: [/p][p][/p][h1][b]SYSTEM UPDATES[/b][/h1][h2][b]Improved Mission Timer[/b][/h2][p]We've updated the mission timer to better communicate what's happening during a run.[/p][list][*][p]Overall clearer timer feedback and readability[/p][/*][*][p]The last section is now visually distinct to communicate urgency[/p][/*][*][p]Optional numerical countdown showing exactly when Reaperworms will appear
[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]Assault Pace Selection[/b][/h2][p]You can now choose your preferred Assault Pace directly from the Mission Map. These impact the time you have to complete each level and mission XP rewards. Base reward values have been adjusted to accommodate the changes. We have also added new Tasks in the OpsCom terminal for each Pace.[/p][list][*][p][b]Cautious[/b] – Lower time pressure[/p][/*][*][p][b]Standard[/b] – Current experience[/p][/*][*][p][b]Reckless[/b] – Higher time pressure
[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]R.E.P.D. Upgrading Improvements[/b][/h2][p]Upgrading at the R.E.P.D. has been streamlined for both Expenite and Spectre Core upgrades.[/p][olist][*][p]When an upgrade is available, a button will appear on the R.E.P.D.[/p][/*][*][p]Any Reclaimer can press it to initiate the upgrade negotiation process[/p][/*][*][p]An upgrade link will be established with all Reclaimers, allowing them to upgrade immediately regardless of their location in the facility
 [/p][/*][/olist][h2][b]Upgrade Negotiation Rework[/b][/h2][p]We've made several improvements to upgrade drafts and player choice. We have really been enjoying these changes ourselves and are excited for you to try them out, and hear what you think.[/p][list][*][p]When a player selects an upgrade, it is replaced with a new option, ensuring everyone gets the same number of choices[/p][/*][*][p]The "Skip for Health" option has been removed[/p][/*][*][p]Health upgrades now appear alongside all other upgrades[/p][/*][*][p]All upgrades within a draft now share the same rarity
[/p][/*][/list][p]We have also tweaked many of the existing upgrades, changing some of them extensively and removing others to make every choice feel exciting and worthwhile. This will be an ongoing process and we are also working on new upgrades that will be added in later updates.[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h1][b]NEW CONTENT[/b][/h1][h2][b]New Weapons[/b][/h2][list][*][p][b]Trident[/b] – Direct Energy Shotgun
A new weapon from the makers of the DRAK 25 the Trident offers two firing modes. Standard fire is a semi-automatic 3-shot blast. While holding down the trigger will charge up a massive barrage for dealing with groups of targets.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Corrosive Sludge Pump[/b] – Heavy Weapon
Cover the corespawn with sticky corrosive goo. Offering a mix of crowd control and continuous damage over time. The mixture is also very potent at melting enemy armor. The weapon can be charged to lob a large projectile saturating an area in corrosive sludge.
[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]New Enemy[/b][/h2][p][b]Voidkin Drifter[/b] – A brand-new flying threat to expand the combat variety. Highly mobile and hard to hit, the Drifter will only stop to charge up its attack. While the Void Bolts it launches may be relatively slow they pack a heavy punch, so watch out and don’t get surrounded.
[/p][h2][b]New Risk Vectors[/b][/h2][p]We have added 3 new Risk Vectors to the pool, one negative and two positives.[/p][list][*][p]Drifter Surge - Bring in groups of the new Voidkin for you to battle[/p][/*][*][p]Bio-Booster - Adds a second Bio-Booster to the level[/p][/*][*][p]Work Bench - Adds a second Work Bench to the level
[/p][/*][/list][p][b]New Core Biome (DELAYED)[/b][/p][p]Our goal is to introduce a unique Core biome for each end boss.[/p][p]With Update 1, we're adding a new Core biome for [b]The Ramok[/b]. For now, [b]Molaktula[/b] will also use this biome until its own unique environment arrives in a future update.
[/p][h2][b]New Mining Constructions[/b][/h2][p]13 new mining constructions are being added to facilities, bringing greater variety to facility exploration. Final count will depend on how many more we get done over the following days.
[/p][h2][b]New OpsCom Deployments and Tasks[/b][/h2][p]We have added 2 new deployments to the OpsCom terminal. Both allow progression without requiring total mission success.[/p][list][*][p]Eliminate Corespawn -Tracked as a team and not individual kills[/p][/*][*][p]Clear Facility Levels - Sometimes just making it one level deeper is a hard-fought win.[/p][/*][/list][p]We have also added 3 new Tasks, one for each Assault Pace.
[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h1][b]WEAPON BALANCE[/b][/h1][p]We're making a broad pass on weapon balance to create a more consistent difficulty floor across the game.[/p][list][*][p]All starting weapons are now common but come with 2 attributes[/p][/*][*][p]Work Benches now have a chance for offering higher rarity weapons[/p][/*][*][p]Heavy Weapon Crates now have a wider rarity range[/p][/*][*][p]Individual weapons are getting balance tweaks as well but this will be an ongoing process and feedback is always appreciated.[/p][/*][*][p]Additionally, several harder-to-master weapons (like the Shock Striker and Devastator) have been moved from the Starting Weapon Pool to the Workbench, allowing new players to ease into the experience more naturally.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][h1][b]MISCELLANEOUS[/b][/h1][list][*][p]An additional Munitions Crate has been added to each Facility level to improve ammo economy[/p][/*][*][p]More Red Sugar has been added throughout the caves to help offset the removal of "Skip for Health"[/p][/*][*][p]Free Leaf Lovers at the bar[/p][/*][*][p]New Tracks for the Jukebox: Disco, Smooth Soul, Funk, Soul[/p][/*][*][p]Stacking of enhancements for better overview in Loadout Terminal[/p][/*][*][p]Auto-equip highest tier enhancements when unlocking new enhancements[/p][/*][*][p]Added several autosprint modes you can toggle in the Settings. [/p][/*][/list][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p]Rock and Stone![/p][p][i]With Love,[/i][/p][p][i]- The Ghost Ship Crew[/i][/p][p]
[/p]

newsitems.title: Day-after reflections: addressing your feedback
newsitems.author: GSG Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/54c297973ebc68de16baf8d6a9b98a9ccab15912.jpg[/img]

[h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1]

Hell of a day, huh?

It’s been a rollercoaster of a launch and we’ve gotten lots of feedback, both positive and negative. We’re taking both seriously. We’re currently working on a patch for today with some “safe” smaller improvements, and cooking up a plan to address more major points of critique in the immediate future.

Thanks to everybody who’s been part of this launch — both for your enthusiasm, and for letting us know how we can make Rogue Core better. 

Busy days ahead! Let’s get into it.

[hr][/hr]
[h2][b]Smaller short-term fixes coming in a patch today[/b][/h2]

There’s a whole lot of feedback to process, and much of it has to do with systems that are pretty deeply baked into how Rogue Core is designed. Those will take a bit of time to tackle. But we’ve identified some stuff closer to the surface that we can fix right now to help smooth out and improve people’s first impressions of the game.

Later today we’ll be rolling out a day-one hotfix focusing on smaller, “safe” fixes. Basically, stuff we can do right now without setting everything else on fire.

In that, you can expect:
[list]
[*] [b]Improvements to the tutorial:[/b] Reducing the post-processing effects during the tutorial, and clearly mentioning the photosensitivity toggle in settings. Also, more clearly explaining the Workbench/Toolbox system (more tutorial improvements coming later).
[*] [b]Difficulty tweaks:[/b] Smoothing out the new player’s experience by extending time limits on Depths 1 and 2, and slowing down enemy spawns in the critical threat level
[*] [b]Bug fixes:[/b] Standard stuff here; preventing crashes, softlocks, other high-priority issues
[*] [b]Musical diversions:[/b] Adding 3 new tracks to the Jukebox (Jazz, Jungle & Blues)
[/list]These will be coming in a few hours, and we'll post the full patchnotes here on Steam.

[h2][b]Key frustrations: timer, shared upgrades, and ammo[/b][/h2]

When we look at what people don’t like about Rogue Core, three main pain points stand out:
[olist]
[*] Lots of people think the timer isn’t fun.
[*] Shared upgrades can be frustrating and interrupt the flow of the game.
[*] Ammo economy is a big issue.
[/olist]These certainly aren’t the only issues we’re seeing, but they do seem to be the biggest. Both in that they’re mentioned most frequently, and they take the most fun out of the experience. So we’re making them our immediate priority.

We don’t want to just rush out a knee-jerk panic fix for these things. It’ll take a second for us to reflect on how to improve them, and then to build and test those improvements. It’s not an overnight fix, but it is our main focus right now.

We’ll update you once we’ve got more here. Until then, you can trust that we hear you loud and clear, and we’re working on it.

[h2][b]Roadmap coming tomorrow[/b][/h2]

In light of your feedback, we’re changing up our roadmap. We want to focus on the stuff that’s most feasible for us to fix quickly, that’ll make the biggest difference for people who don’t feel like Rogue Core is up to their expectations.

We’ll post that tomorrow here on Steam. That ought to give you a clearer picture of how we’ll go about developing Rogue Core from here, and what to expect from us in the weeks and months to come. 

[hr][/hr]
All of us, laying aside any gripes or praises, want Rogue Core to be the best it can be. Early Access is just square one, and we’re excited to see how the game grows from here.

Hope everybody’s doing well. Talk soon!

[i]With love,
-The Ghost Ship crew
[/i]

newsitems.title: Reclaimer Handbook: Tactical tips to survive your first deployment
newsitems.author: GSG Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/73cc0ec219d2b2f4074a12b87bbbc31943aca045.jpg[/img]

[h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1]

Tomorrow, we take back Hoxxes.

Some of you may be veteran miners, having faithfully served this Company in the mines of Hoxxes IV. Others may be newly-enlisted, deploying to the depths for the first time.

Operations Command has assembled this tactical briefing to help you get the most of your Rogue Core experience and make sure you return back to the Ramrod in one piece. If you plan on deploying with other Reclaimers, Management asks that you share this resource with your squadmates as recommended reading. Proper training will help us minimize casualties on our first day of Operation Rogue Core.

[hr][/hr]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/91b43e49e87b356e71f23b18a8f9302a4ff8b118.png[/img]
[h2][b]1. Always keep an eye on your mission timer. [/b][/h2]

In Rogue Core, time is the biggest enemy of them all. You’ll be under pressure from the moment you step out of the Drop Pod, and managing your time is crucial for your survival. If you let the timer run out, you’ll enter Threat Level Critical — meaning the Core Spawn will throw everything they’ve got at you until you’re dead or gone. 

As you fight through each level of the mine, you should [b]aim to extract with time to spare.[/b] Otherwise you’ll have to deal with the Reaperworms.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/08e66181994c44b757ba9fc518891875c66c6c44.png[/img][h2][b]2. Prioritize locating the elevator.[/b][/h2]

[b]The elevator is your extraction point.[/b] It’s your ticket out of any level, and your only way of progressing further. As soon as you deploy, you should be focused on finding the next elevator. There will be a power cable leading from one elevator to the next, so you can use this as your trail of breadcrumbs.

Calling the elevator will trigger an enemy attack, so you should be grouped up and prepared for combat before you do this. You should also find as many upgrades and resources as you can before calling the elevator —  but don’t wait too long.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/2a7b6f7e4deda8bd964b9143aeec702670ea600f.png[/img]
[h2][b]3. A.C.E. - Always Collect Expenite.[/b][/h2]

The wünder-mineral Expenite is [b]your key to earning powerful new upgrades[/b] during missions. If you’re used to Deep Rock Galactic, you can think of it like Nitra — a mineral you should always collect and deposit at every opportunity.

Expenite can be found in natural deposits within the mines, as well as side objectives (such as abandoned heavy machinery) you may encounter during missions.

Depositing enough Expenite in the Remote Expenite Processing Drone (R.E.P.D.) will earn you an upgrade. You’ll need to group up with your team and select these cooperatively. You don’t need to do this every single time you earn one — they will stack up, and you can claim several in a row. Time it with your team to get the best effect.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/f5186291fa8eb93ec779392df5ac4862a146afa7.png[/img][h2][b]4. Make use of Workbenches and Bio-Boosters. [/b][/h2]

Workbenches and Bio-Boosters will be found on every level of the mine. They’re a [b]surefire way to get stronger weapons[/b] and more powerful abilities, in addition to what you’ll earn from Expenite upgrades. Your enemies will be getting stronger, so you need to keep up.

Both these resources require a small unlock process to become active. Remember to ping these resources for teammates when you find them — it’d be a shame to extract before you collect your upgrade.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/9f39ebeb10483af079fd42d10ea64708f26b720b.png[/img]
[h2][b]5. Don't expect to win your first run. [/b][/h2]

[b]The baseline difficulty of Rogue Core is harder than Deep Rock Galactic.[/b] We’d say it starts somewhere close to Hazard 3 difficulty. Failure is part of this game. But unlike Deep Rock Galactic, Rogue Core doesn’t penalize failure as much. You’ll still collect rewards and progression proportional to your progress. We’ll just bio-print some new organs in the Med Bay, glue you back together, and you’re ready for another go.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/62b88815d0f90fca3d385579d941e01c64103c06.png[/img][h2][b]6. You can (and should) upgrade your Reclaimers between missions.[/b][/h2]

Rogue Core is a rogue[i]lite[/i] game, meaning you have permanent player progression. When you complete missions (or if you die trying), you’ll earn Reclaimer Points, which unlock [b]Merits and Enhancement Chips.[/b] You can spend Merit points to unlock upgrade slots for your character build, and Enhancement Chips unlock the upgrades to insert in these slots. This allows you to start every run with boosted stats. 

As you progress, you’ll unlock more upgrades and more sockets — giving you more options to fine-tune your build exactly for the strengths you want.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/cedcfcd225d79ced9a33900a1d0ad7cefce959d1.png[/img][h2][b]7. Confiscate Security Cameras whenever possible.[/b][/h2]

As per company policy, all Deep Rock Galactic mining facilities are equipped with security cameras. These cameras monitor employee behavior and deter wage theft, but also contain oxygen and contaminant monitoring devices to ensure a safe working environment.

Until Management has a full understanding of the Grayout incident, the sensitive data in these cameras must be handled with the utmost discretion. Collect them whenever you come across them, and [b]Management will reward you[/b] with a multiplier for your Reclaimer Points issued at the end of a mission.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/acac0003f18dc2e99b581c357c7c89468f1144b1.png[/img][h2][b]8. Intel is your key to game progression.[/b][/h2]

Intel represents our understanding of the Grayout anomaly and Expenite research. You must collect Intel by completing specific Intel Tasks during missions. These tasks can be viewed, tracked and unlocked via the side panel in the Mission Terminal aboard the Ramrod.

As you collect more Intel, OMEGA will grant you an increased Clearance Level. Certain Clearance Levels are required to access more challenging missions, new biomes, and to activate resources and equipment in the mining facilities.

A diligent Reclaimer must always remember to [b]complete Intel Tasks whenever possible[/b], and redeem them to unlock new access privileges.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/189ded3490d2d82b47af57a5fb2185e932bb6ecb.png[/img]
[h2][b]9. Remember the Reclaimer Handbook.[/b][/h2]

Knowledge is a Reclaimer’s most powerful weapon (if you don’t count guns, pickaxes, fists, grenades, superheated energy blades or electric shock drones). As such, it’s important you remember to refer to your [b]Reclaimer Handbook[/b] to better understand your mission as well as your opponents.

You can expect to unlock new entries in the Handbook as you progress through Rogue Core. Some of these entries might contain useful hints and information. You can access the Handbook via the terminals in your personal cabin, or from the ESC menu. 

[hr][/hr]
On behalf of Management, we’d like to thank you for joining the Reclaimers, and being the first to the front in Operation Rogue Core. When you deploy, know that you do so with the support of the Company behind you.

We look forward to following your progress, and to restoring Hoxxes IV to full operating capacity. 

Good luck tomorrow, Reclaimer. [b]Rock and Stone.[/b]

[i]With love,
The Ghost Ship Crew[/i]

newsitems.title: Pre-launch: What Rogue Core is and isn’t
newsitems.author: GSG Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/aa51a062af9ef78f0efb20a9d4f1930648b803be.jpg[/img]

[h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1]

We’re now two days away from Rogue Core’s Early Access launch! The game will go live on Steam on [b]May 20th[/b] at [b]18:00 CEST[/b]. 

Ahead of that, we wanted to share a few thoughts on the whole early access process, our plan for the months after launch, and what Rogue Core is all about.

[hr][/hr]
[h2][b]Rogue Core isn’t Deep Rock Galactic[/b][/h2]

We developed this game as a standalone title to explore a different pace and playstyle, and to build up new gameplay mechanics and progression structures. It’s not a DLC for a lot of reasons, but a big one is that if we tried to fold all this new stuff back into Deep Rock Galactic, we’d dilute that game’s identity. Rogue Core is a spinoff, not a sequel. It’s intended to scratch a different itch than DRG, and to co-exist alongside it.

Rogue Core does come from Deep Rock Galactic’s DNA, but it plays much differently. 
Here are the three key ways it differs from DRG:
[list]
[*] [b]It's faster-paced.[/b] You’re under more pressure, and time is a resource you need to manage. Each level is on a mission timer, and you may not be able to complete every single side objective before your time runs out and you reach critical threat level.
[*] [b]It's harder and more intense.[/b] The baseline difficulty is more challenging. We’d say the game probably starts close to the 'Hazard 3' experience from Deep Rock Galactic, and it scales up from there. 
[*] [b]There's more focus on combat.[/b] In Rogue Core, the cave generation is more linear. Where DRG had more focus on traversal and terrain modification, Rogue Core introduces fighting in and around industrial structures in the caves.
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/072900647da9f43b9c0f5094596e6896056b7c68.png[/img]
[h2][b]Early access is just the beginning[/b][/h2]

We've done our best to polish what we've got, but this is just the beginning of Rogue Core. We’ve still got a big long wishlist of things to improve, add and adjust.

Heading into our Early Access launch, it’s inevitable that folks will compare Rogue Core against Deep Rock Galactic. We do it too. But it's worth remembering that Deep Rock Galactic has had about ten years' more development than Rogue Core. [url=https://youtu.be/IkUsPpOPIss?si=Waml_yX9AWxJ_6ZS]Here’s the trailer from right before DRG released to early access[/url], for some perspective on how far it’s come since then.

Granted, we’ve grown a bit ourselves, and today’s standard for early access isn’t the same as it was in 2018. But the principle remains: this version of Rogue Core is a starting point. How it evolves from here depends a lot on what you have to say about it. 

Here are just a couple examples of what we could work on in the coming months:
[list]
[*] More weapons, equipment and grenades
[*] New enemies and bosses
[*] More Expenite Upgrades and Artifacts
[*] New sub-objectives and side encounters
[*] More intricate “Core Biome” features/terrain generation
[/list]
We’re working on a new Early Access Living Roadmap, to give an idea of our biggest priorities for post-EA development and a general timeline. We expect to have that out on the 20th when the game goes live.

As always, keep in mind that our roadmaps can change. Maybe there’s some roadwork up ahead, or a cool detour. You never know.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/e11aba41f4a8fe8b09c560d20279b88da2af7f09.png[/img]

[h2][b]We’re eager to hear what you think![/b][/h2]

We want to hear your thoughts: the good, the bad and the ugly.

What's new, fresh and exciting? What's clunky and frustrating? What’s unexpected in a good way, and what’s unexpected in a bad way? All of it matters, and all of it helps us plan our next steps. 

Any game, and especially one in early access, is gonna get its fair share of critique. That's fair enough. We think what we’ve got now is good, but there’s always room for improvement. 

If you’ve got feedback, here are the best ways to make your voice heard:
[list]
[*] On our official Discord
[*] On the Rogue Core subreddit
[*] Making a Youtube video essay
[*] Tuning in to chat on our weekly dev streams
[/list]If you’ve got anything super mean and unconstructive to say, we prefer that sent as a physical letter so that we’ve got your mailing address. <3

All that said, we’ve been thrilled to see all the feedback and excitement surrounding Rogue Core. Our early access release date has felt like an abstract concept for so long, it’s a trippy feeling to realize it’s a concrete date — and soon. We’re excited to hear your thoughts on all of it, and to see where the path ahead takes us.

[hr][/hr]
Finally, we’d just like to send you a whole lot of love from our whole team. After so many years in development, it’s pretty wild to finally send this game out in the world. Many many thanks for all your interest, curiosity, support and suggestions along the way. 

We’ll see you down in the mines. [b]Rock and Stone![/b]

[i]With love,
-The Ghost Ship Crew[/i]

newsitems.title: Want to help Rogue Core speak your language?
newsitems.author: GSG_Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/9fb7cb095b36090650a6d36969b27208a6417db7.jpg"][/img]
[/p][h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1][p]
What’s the Slovak word for ‘Core Spawn Clamorhead’?
Can OMEGA learn to speak Korean?  
Is a Spanish Reclaimer a [i]Recuperador[/i] or a [i]Reclamero[/i]? 

Making a video game involves a lot of made-up terminology. And that’s all good fun, until those words run into the contextual and grammatical complexities of all the world’s languages. It takes a lot to make sure a game makes sense beyond its mother tongue.

And we want Rogue Core to speak your language.

Localizing Rogue Core is largely driven by volunteer translators from the community. On some occasions, we’ll get some help from a professional translation agency for certain languages. But a professional crew never really knows the full context of the game: You can translate “health” as a word, but you’re missing how Health works as a game mechanic. The polish and detail, the nuance that really brings each language to life, comes from the community. 

That’s where you come in. After all, it’s the players that know the game best. You know the world, the lore, all the in-jokes. You’re able to spot little contextual inconsistencies and game mechanics that a professional translator might gloss over. 

With Deep Rock Galactic, community translators are helping bring the game into 39 different languages, even including the constructed language Esperanto. Rogue Core is next up, and there’s lots to do as we push toward Early Access. Right now, there are a few dozen translators working to bring Rogue Core into 32 different languages and counting. 

We want you as the next one to join the team.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/a7432a0e2e774a24535f12c04e397224b73b126c.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]Why help translate?[/h1][p]
Community translators do it for the love of the game. 

Discord user Drakoniid is one of the community’s translator managers. Over the past six years, they’ve helped translate Deep Rock Galactic and Rogue Core into French, and are now part of coordinating the overall translation project across all languages. 

As they tell it, translating lets them make their mark on a game that means a lot to them, and share that interest with others.

“Since I got involved, I ended up meeting most of the French translation team and have become real-life friends with them now. Playing Deep Rock Galactic and the connections I made there did a lot for me to socialize and overcome anxiety. I just really love the game and all the work put into it, and translating is my way to help improve it and spread it further.”

Part of it is also the satisfaction of a good translation. Take DRG’s Caretaker, for example. The most direct French translation for “caretaker” is [i]gardien[/i], but that doesn’t quite have the same razzle-dazzle. Plus, the Glyphid Warden is already called the [i]gardien[/i] in French. So the French translators came up with an original name: [i]le cerbère-nétique[/i]. It combines Cerberus, the mythical three-headed hellhound, with “cybernetic”.

It’s this level of granular familiarity that only fans of the game have, and what puts community translators a cut above any professional service. Games get a level of depth and detail that more native speakers can appreciate.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/e2d1a8f0cd874eda69f3388308abd0f2a036392a.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]How to get involved[/h1][p]
If you’re interested in Rogue Core and your native language is something other than English, we could use your help. You can become part of the game’s development, and make it shine in your own language.

Joining the translation team is easy and you don’t need any prior experience. If you were to start right after reading this, you could be translating text in Rogue Core just fifteen minutes from now.

Here’s all you need to do to get started:
[/p][olist][*][p] Head over to [url="https://crowdin.com/project/drg-rogue-core"]CrowdIn[/url], our translation portal.
[/p][/*][*][p] Make an account there (just requires an email address).
[/p][/*][*][p] Open up the Rogue Core project, select your desired language, and either open the [b]AllGameText[/b] file, or click [b]TranslateAll[/b].
[/p][/*][*][p] Select a string of text for the game and submit your translation.
[/p][/*][/olist][p]That’s it! That’s the whole process of translating text. 

If you’d like to do it as a regular thing and connect with other volunteer translators for your language, head to the [url="http://discord.gg/drg"]official Deep Rock Galactic Discord[/url] and go to the [b]#babelfish-lounge[/b] channel and check out the channel description and pinned posts.

Hope to see you there!

[i]Kærlig hilsen,
-Besætningen på Spøgelsesskibet[/i]
[/p]

newsitems.title: Dev Peek: Cosmetics! and how we name them
newsitems.author: GSG_Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/3a221d046e0082554e3897912571dd0a7a2c27c5.jpg[/img]

[h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1]

Another little dev peek! This time, we’re taking a look at character cosmetics.

We initially weren’t going to do much in the way of cosmetics for Rogue Core, but then we realized there’s no fun in that. So now we’re doing them.

Cosmetics begin in the art department. Our 2D and 3D artists start the process, coming up with loads of drafts for all sorts of cosmetics we could put in each category. They talk with the Game Designers to decide which cosmetic categories we’ll have. There’s at least one new cosmetic category in Rogue Core: We’re adding piercings.

A lot of the initial drafting process is just throwing ideas at the wall and seeing what sticks. But there’s also the question of how to fit the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/2605790/announcements/detail/534345939582715198?snr=2___]established Reclaimer aesthetic[/url]. And of course, whether these ideas would really work in the game. Do we like the look? Would it be tricky to implement, or clip with any character models? Can we do multicolored beards, or is that too tricky to categorize?

https://steamcommunity.com/games/2605790/announcements/detail/534345939582715198?snr=2___
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/9e25ff693e2b5b19c1b0282b85a6abcec12c7d0e.png[/img][i]Some early-stage concepts for various beards, hair and mustaches.[/i]

Ultimately, the Art Director and Game Director make the final call on what ideas get into the game or not. Once that’s settled, the collection of 2D and 3D drafts get made into their polished, in-game versions.

Once the cosmetics are made, they all need names. 3D Artist Harpa went and put all the new cosmetics into a big spreadsheet (see below), which serves as the Naming Factory. 

Naming cosmetics is mostly a gut-feeling thing. It feels sort of like an improv game, maybe something from Whose Line Is It Anyway. See the picture, think up a catchy name. Whatever comes to mind. Maybe the cosmetic reminds me of some movie or fun cultural reference, so I’ll try to make that fit. Maybe there’s some good alliteration, or a silly joke to be made. Maybe it’s best not to make a joke, and just be descriptive. No overthinking allowed, just have fun with it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/3418811bf95c174987e22468e4a396ebbbdfdd14.png[/img]
The final step is implementation: Connecting these names and descriptions to the assets in Unreal, and making sure everything is where it ought to be in the game.

You can expect these new cosmetics (and their names) to make an appearance in the next Closed Alpha playtest for Rogue Core. More news on that playtest is coming next week. Keep an eye on the Steam page.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Early Access release date to be announced this Thursday[/h2]

Oh right! Before we go, some news:

We'll be announcing the Early Access release date for Rogue Core later this week. 

This announcement comes with its own brand-new trailer, which will premiere as part of the [url=https://www.futuregamesshow.com/about]2026 Future Games Show Spring Showcase[/url] this [b]Thursday, March 12th[/b] at [b]21:00 CET[/b] (that’s around lunchtime if you’re in North America).

If you’d like to catch the live release date reveal, you’ll need to tune in to the Future Games Show. It will broadcast on [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iJQzdmAWyR4]Youtube[/url], [url=https://m.twitch.tv/futuregamesshow/about]Twitch[/url], Twitter, Steam and BiliBili. We’ll share the trailer on our own channels (like here on Steam) some hours after the event. Probably on Friday.

That's all for now. Rock and Stone!

[i]With love,
-The Ghost Ship Crew[/i]

newsitems.title: Dev Peek: Memorial Hall + OMEGA lines
newsitems.author: GSG_Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/b77395bb2ecebce427a63f436913801bac7b294f.png[/img]

[h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1]

Back with another update on Rogue Core’s development! But this won’t be the usual Dev Diary format. In fact, we’re changing things up.

There’s loads to do as we push toward Early Access, which means our writing team (me) doesn’t have as much time to work on Dev Diary posts. Moving ahead, we’ll focus on Dev Peeks (genius name), which are gonna be shorter, more focused, and more frequent. Exactly how frequent remains to be seen.

Until we get our Writer Cloning Machine working, this is how we’ll balance our own needs for in-game writing with keeping you all updated on what we’re up to.

Figuring out how to do this feels like the picture below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/832dc2adfcd59a51029e13f88107b1ecbe03bfe7.png[/img]
[h2]Writing voice lines[/h2]

Confronting a real-deal Early Access launch means that the thousands of placeholder texts scribbled down over the past few years all need proofreading, and fast. That means tooltips, the reference manual, tutorial texts, everything.

It also involves finding areas where we still need voicelines (from dwarves or OMEGA), and writing lines so we still have time to get them recorded.

Down below is a peek at the document we use for writing and archiving all our voicelines. We have one for dwarves and one for OMEGA. They're just regular old spreadsheets, spooling down for thousands of rows.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/5d592063e05987d8c6c972e7a26f383294054fc7.jpg[/img]

Here’s how the process works:
[list]
[*] The Game Design team flags a need for a voice prompt ([i]“We want to guide players to check their Intel progression system regularly, and reward them for collecting Intel. Maybe OMEGA could say something when you get back from a mission?”[/i])
[*] Writer comes up with lines that meet this purpose. You need to come up with a lot of variations, more than you’d think. This is so that it doesn’t sound repetitive when that line prompt comes up multiple times.
[*] Writer sanity-checks this with the Game Designers, to make sure we’re accurately representing how the game systems actually work.
[*] Writer, who in this case is also the voice of OMEGA, goes in and records the lines in our sound studio, with the help of Sound Engineer.
[*] Sound Engineer then masters and filters the voice, and hooks it up into the game, so the lines cue at the appropriate time.
[*] Development team playtests on regular intervals, and lets us know if the lines are cool or if they suck. In the case of the latter, we revise and redo them.
[/list]So far, OMEGA has just under 1,000 lines written, and the dwarves already have a couple thousand lines. It’ll keep growing, though.

[h2]The Ramrod's Memorial Hall (WIP)[/h2]

One spot where we're writing and testing voicelines is for the new Memorial Hall. Still unsure of how that whole process is going to work, and the hall itself is still WIP. But here’s a first look at the space:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/d3c7fd0c7e24d405c04e6fcdef18776563dcd8f1.png[/img]
Okay that’s it for this one! Hopefully we can announce a Playtest 06 one of these days. Maybe this coming month? Nothing locked in yet though. Stay tuned.

See you soon. Rock and Stone, Reclaimers.

[i]With love,
-The Ghost Ship Crew[/i]

newsitems.title: Development Diary: January 2026
newsitems.author: GSG_Aaron
newsitems.contents:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/1b0a0fb5fbe85fe26915c6b4d17b59361ef93bab.jpg[/img]

[h1]Hello Reclaimers,[/h1]

We’re back in full swing after the holiday break, pushing ever closer toward early access. It’s been a productive month for us, too! Fun feeling to see new details start to shine, and to get bigger game features working the way we want.

[b]IN THIS ISSUE:[/b]
[list]
[*] Playtest 06 when?
[*] Upgrading the Ramrod’s bar + fitness area
[*] A very special cave construction
[*] We might have figured out late joining
[/list]As usual, [u][b]everything in here reflects a work in progress[/b][/u]. Please keep in mind that what we show and talk about here can (and very likely will) change before we reach early access.

Cool! Let’s get after it.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]News on the next playtest[/h2]

First up, a question we get a lot.

Many folks have been asking and speculating (and understandably so) about whether we’ll do another playtest before Rogue Core launches in early access.

The answer is yes!

But before you light the celebratory fireworks, we should say we don’t quite know when yet. It mostly depends on how quickly we can shift gears from “implement a bunch of stuff” to “fix the bugs and crashes” mode. Right now, we’re still focused on building up new stuff. So it’ll be several weeks at the very least before we look at another playtest. 

When we do open up for the next playtest (and send out a new wave of invites), we’ll announce it here on Steam. So you don’t need to go checking your inbox until you see that post.

As always, selection for the playtests is entirely random, and invites are sent out via Steam. For more questions on how it all works, we’ll refer you to our handy Closed Alpha FAQ article right here.

https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2605790/view/574879683755115309
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Beers + weightlifting on the Ramrod[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/c2eeb60653218e5c1ada87f116ce8b1b659830d8.jpg[/img]
One big focus this month has been tightening up the gameplay loop for the fitness area and bar aboard the Reclaimer’s ship, the RV-09 Ramrod.

While the carefree miners of Deep Rock Galactic simply order their beers with their wages, the Reclaimers do things a little different. If you want to drink on the Ramrod, you gotta hit the gym first. Lifting weights puts you in a caloric deficit, which enables you to order up a round of beers from OMEGA. Strict stuff on this ship.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/3be75e0aef784784cfbb2a176153882b55c0a7e6.jpg[/img]
Don’t worry, you don’t have to do very much. But you do have to do some, because there is no place for weakness among Reclaimers.

Implementing this whole system has required our game designers to cook up specific little ‘minigames’ for each lift available at the gym, our artists to animate it all and make UI overlays, our writers (hello!) to write voicelines for everything, and our voice actors (hello again) to record it all. Then our sound guys make sure all the voicelines are hooked up and play at the right time. Oh, and of course then our QA team has to test everything, and our programmers have to fix anything they find. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/c42f4274f4723f682c5b97d85af4cdbe7836f553.jpg[/img]
All this is to say, there’s a lot more work than you’d expect in this relatively minor part of the game. And still a good bit to do in terms of polishing details like animations, UI and the points system.

Hopefully it’ll be ready by the time Playtest 06 rolls around. I’m optimistic.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Bringing the GSG office to Rogue Core[/h2]

As you likely know by now, the cave systems of Rogue Core aren’t just organic caverns. They’re also populated with loads of manmade (dwarfmade, rather) constructions like scaffolding and giant machinery and carved-out rooms, to give the mining facilities a detailed, lived-in feel.

A week or two ago, one of our 3D artists Arvid (formerly [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/DeepRockGalactic/announcements/detail/4110170432168891298]loot bug keeper[/url]) came up with an excellent idea: Recreate part of the real-life Ghost Ship Games office as a cave construction in Rogue Core.

So now, while down in the mines, there’s a chance you’ll come across an “employee canteen” sort of room, which is in fact a replica of the top floor of our Copenhagen office.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/9d8bb56f8f37bec8bba70de7e87e0d146d94dbbd.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/bd2db5f81503f664d75d6009e7261d37e5c16467.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/a1bc6505cc4efa9e5400a01530db89df9a3d0e88.jpg[/img]
In real life, it’s where we eat lunch, have meetings, and broadcast our weekly dev streams. Maybe the DRG mining teams use their version in a similar way.

Embedded right below is a quick walk-through of the new room. You can also revisit the shots of the fifth floor from our [url=https://youtu.be/L1LzygOXKbg?si=8Mvb35shXrnF2bcb]office tour video[/url], in case you want to compare them.

[previewyoutube=U6vmNtpGTps;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/fba29d5839c48d84a468bd799bc002d96f2d9aeb.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Testing late joining solutions[/h2]

One of your biggest community asks during development has been regarding the possibility of late joining lobbies. So far, we haven’t had it in any form. But we might have figured out a solution.

We’re working on some mechanics to allow late joining to a certain extent. It won’t be that people can join at any stage -- in all likelihood, it'll probably something allowing people to join up until the end of the first stage of the facility.

There are two tricky factors that kept us from looking at this earlier, and they still create some challenges as we put this system in place.
[olist]
[*] [b]Game balance.[/b] What do we do for late players in terms of upgrades? Should they get to pick, or just get a bunch of random ones? Is it still fun if you spawn in with a jumble of several facility levels’ worth of random upgrades? Gotta find the balance between what’s feasible and what’s fun here.
[*] [b]Technical limitations.[/b] This is the backend stuff, like how a new player’s computer links up with the rest of the team and loads in new levels without causing crashes, desyncs or weird client/host discrepancies.
[/olist]So right now it’s more of an intention than a working prototype. But once we’ve got something together, we’ll test it out and let you know how it works. In any case, our big idea is for new dwarves to spawn in at a bathroom down in the mining facilities, for the ironclad plot continuity that the late dwarf simply took a long time on the toilet.

To wrap things up, here’s a look at the toilet we’re working on. Let us know in the comments what you think the Reclaimers are eating that would make this design necessary.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44682613/5d20092641e9a9b42bddc9fa83472f2be69fa35e.gif[/img]
[hr][/hr]
So there’s our month in a nutshell. We’ve been busy over here on several fronts – in case you didn’t notice, Season 06 of Deep Rock Galactic comes out tomorrow! Be sure to give it a spin when you can.

Take care out there, and talk to you soon.

[i]With love,
-The Ghost Ship Crew[/i]

newsitems.contents:
